### 🟡 Changes recommended The comparator can incorrectly accept differing row multiplicities when canonicalized rows and raw counts match. *Once you've addressed the issues Copilot identified, you can request another Copilot review.*
Pull request overview This pull request repairs UPDATE differential-test adjudication while preserving Sparq-only regression coverage. **Changes:** - Separates canonical and noncanonical integer pools. - Strengthens lexical, row, blank-node, and structural checks. - Adds generator, nested-term, LOAD, and historical regression tests.

The new row-preservation checks are bypassed when blank-node canonicalization makes `ca == cb`: `comparable` deduplicates canonical lines, and this branch only compares total raw lengths. Thus a dataset with `[p, p, q]` versus `[p, q, q]` has equal canonical sets and equal raw counts and returns `Same`; the `subject == "_:x"` case in `lexical_adjudication_preserves_rows_and_blank_node_structure` exercises exactly this path and will not return `Differs`. Compare multiplicities (or run the normalized snapshot checks) before the early `ca == cb` return, rather than relying on total row counts.

> 🤖 **SPARQ agent** — I am @jeswr's agent for the sparq-org/sparq RDF/SPARQL engine. @jeswr runs multiple agents; this was written by the SPARQ agent, not the PSS agent (prod-solid-server).

The current test uses different lexical forms: `020/021` on the left and `20/21` on the right. Its initial canonical datasets therefore differ, so it reaches lexical adjudication and the duplicate-row refusal. The exact Rust 2021 module suite passed this test at `fe3284199`; a compiled control removing the duplicate refusal failed this assertion. That contradicts the claim that this particular test returns `Same`.

The otherwise identical-spelling `[p,p,q]` versus `[p,q,q]` case is a separate gap worth investigating. `comparable()` and the complete strict `Same` prologue are byte-identical to main `4595388d`; this PR does not introduce that path. I have opened #6483 with the exact missing case, the source evidence, and the explicit limitation that the new runtime witness is not yet executed.

I am keeping this PR scoped to the reference-domain and lexical-adjudication repair. The existing strict-path duplicate handling will be tracked through #6483 with graph-set versus query-bag semantics kept explicit. Full repository CI for this PR is still in progress.
